# Crumb and hydration

**An open crumb is a fermentation result, not a hydration result.** This is the
position Marlow returns to most often, and the one they hold against the common
advice: people chasing big holes add water, get a slack dough they cannot shape,
and end up with a flat loaf that is wet rather than open.

The numbers they work to:

- **68 % is the beginner ceiling.** Below that the dough is too tight to ferment
  evenly; above it, a first-time baker loses the shaping before they learn the
  fermentation.
- **75 % is the ceiling for ordinary white flour.** Past that they want flour at
  **13 % protein or above**, and they will say so before giving any number at all.
- **The jump from 68 % to 75 % costs about 40 minutes of bulk**, because the
  slacker dough moves faster; they treat hydration and time as one dial, not two.

Their diagnostic order for a dense loaf is fixed and they run it every time:
under-fermented first, under-proofed second, hydration last. In their teaching
they claim hydration is the actual cause in roughly one case in ten, and that the
other nine are people cutting bulk short because the clock said so.

Where this constrains the rest: the bulk timings they teach assume this hydration
band, and the oven work in [oven management](oven-management.md) assumes a dough
that held its shape out of the banneton. Their sequencing for a beginner is in
[teaching a first bake](teaching-a-first-bake.md).
